correctness.rationale: On [0,L], the centered product character family has common periodic or antiperiodic endpoint phase, and orthonormality follows by testing differences in the frequency box. Its mean derivative energy is 4π²t(t+2)/12 by isotropic grid variance and unit speed. Bessel occupancies give the sum of the N=(t+1)^d smallest squared Fourier frequencies as a lower bound. Periodic even N costs strictly more; otherwise the strict gap outside the filled band forces finite Fourier support. A finite constant-modulus series has just one exponent by inspecting the largest coefficient lag in its squared modulus. Adjacent-grid ratios and continuity force an affine lift. With signs absorbed, winding digits tile [0,N−1] by distinct sums. A weight 1 must occur; its digits contribute consecutive blocks of t+1 integers that partition the target interval, hence the other weights are multiples of t+1. Divide and iterate. Conversely, reduction modulo t+1 rules out every nonzero box annihilator. The vector is primitive because it has a coordinate ±1, and the orbit count and d=1 endpoint are valid.
residual_risks: The finite computations do not certify arbitrary dimensions or nonlinear curves; the analytic argument does. No other flat metrics or exactness notions were reviewed.
